ticker_news.headline: Western Digital Q3 FY2026 earnings beat: revenue +45% YoY to $3.34B, EPS $2.72 adj vs $2.36 consensus — AI storage demand cited as key driver
WDC stock surged 8.21% on May 5, touching 52-week high of $480.11; +938% over past 12 months
CEO Irving Tan sold 20,000 WDC shares (~$8.24M) on May 1 under a pre-scheduled 10b5-1 plan at $406-$415/share

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Zacks downgraded WDC from strong-buy to hold in early April 2026 citing competition/headwinds. Despite this, current month shows 32 Buy, 3 Hold, 0 Sell ratings from 35 analysts. Consensus avg target ~$413 (range $182-$660 across 23 analysts); WDC is the only major storage name with zero Sell ratings.

web_context.competitor_activity: Storage sector in an AI-driven supercycle. Key rivals: Seagate (HDD-focused, +697% past year), Sandisk (spun out from WDC), Micron and Samsung (NAND/DRAM). Samsung and Micron flagging supply pressure from AI data center demand — broadly positive for WDC pricing power. Seagate focused on high-capacity HDDs for cloud; WDC has broader HDD+NAND exposure. Jim Cramer called the sector 'overheated' but expects further upside. WDC has the strongest analyst backing in the group (22/27 Buy).
